answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a small, time-vested stake that is slashed when peers flag fake identities, instead of trusting a signup form. Like a meadow that only feeds grazers who return season after season, reputation grows from repeated honest work, not from one flashy claim. A ferrous bond, costly to forge and cheap to verify, ties each identity to real compute and history, so spinning up a thousand fables of fake agents costs more than any reward they could drain.
